**The document doesn't give this number.** Figure 7 is included only as an image, and the text never states numeric accuracies by position for the key-value task. The appendix tables of per-position results (Appendix G, p. 18) cover only multi-document QA, not key-value retrieval.

The text does say the following:

- **LongChat-13B (16K) behaves differently at 140 pairs.** It "exhibits a different trend in the 140 key-value setting." When the relevant pair is at the start of the input, it "tends to generate code to retrieve the key, rather than outputting the value directly" (p. 6).
- **Most other models do worst in the middle.** GPT-3.5-Turbo, GPT-3.5-Turbo (16K) and MPT-30B-Instruct have their lowest accuracy when the key is in the middle of the context (p. 6). Models generally struggle at 140 and 300 pairs (p. 6).
- **The only number given is a minimum across all models and settings.** Without query-aware contextualization, the worst-case key-value accuracy is 45.6% (p. 7). The paper doesn't say which model, context length or position this comes from, so it can't be read as LongChat's accuracy at position 70.

To get the value, you'd need to read it from the original Figure 7 plot or from the authors' released results at nelsonliu.me/papers/lost-in-the-middle (p. 2).
